Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

Demonstrated experience in coordinating, performing, and tracking multi-faceted compliance tasks across diverse departments and organizational roles, and ability to work with others from diverse backgrounds.
Experience with policy exception management processes, including reviewing requests and escalating appropriately based on risk thresholds
Familiarity with audit processes and experience coordinating responses for internal and external compliance audits.

The IT Compliance Analyst supports organization-wide compliance with information security Policies, standards, and regulations including internal Policies (IS-3/IS-12), GLBA, HIPAA, FERPA, NSPM-33/CMMC and PCI-DSS through the technical analysis of business practices and the implementation of compliance systems. The position reports to the Chief Information Security Officer and works under the direction of the IT Policy and Compliance Program Manager. The Analyst performs complex technical analysis to maintain institutional data protection and meet evolving regulatory requirements. This role focuses on compliance program operations, audit coordination, metrics tracking, and supports the harmonization of IT services with compliance standards.
Identification of Requirements - 10%

Applies technical expertise and business analysis concepts to identify, evaluate and define IT Compliance program objectives with an understanding of applicable business practices, processes, systems and industry standards to meet business and compliance needs.
Translates established security, privacy, audit, and regulatory requirements into business and system requirements, workflows, controls, and technical specifications
Program Development and Implementation - 30%
Provides technical expertise in developing and implementing IT Compliance systems and procedures.
Creates complex specifications for systems to meet business requirements for IT Compliance activities.
Plans and performs pilots, testing, validation, and user acceptance activities for IT Compliance systems and processes.
Participates in cross-functional teams to address complex business or systems issues affecting IT Compliance.
Performs operational activities associated with IT compliance programs.
Coordinates institutional compliance with information security and disaster recovery policies.
Metrics and Reporting - 20%
Defines data and reporting requirements and develops and maintains key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics related to IT Compliance program effectiveness.
Coordinates data collection for campus and systemwide reporting, and ensures institutional transparency for compliance activities.
Utilizes data visualization tools to design, create, and maintain compliance dashboards and reporting for stakeholders and senior leadership.
Program Evaluation and Improvement - 10%
Gathers, analyzes, prepares and summarizes recommendations for improvement of IT Compliance programs and business processes.
Recommends and implements changes in processes and procedures.
Negotiates with stakeholders on IT Compliance program specifications.
Documentation and Training - 20%
Gathers, analyzes, prepares and summarizes information on IT Compliance programs and business processes, documenting requirements and revising existing system and process logic issues as necessary.
Provides support and training on IT Compliance programs.

Analyzes audit observations and corrective actions and translates them into business, system, process, data, and control requirements. Coordinates evidence collection and tracks implementation of remediation activities.
Professional Development and Other Duties - 5%
Engages in continuous professional development to remain current on emerging technologies, information security and privacy regulations, compliance frameworks, industry standards, and best practices.
Participates in relevant training, professional organizations, and UC systemwide communities to enhance knowledge and effectiveness.
Contributes to departmental and organizational initiatives and performs other related duties and special projects as assigned.
Proficiency in Tableau or similar data analysis software for the purpose of metrics tracking and dashboard creation
Thorough knowledge of business and process analysis functions.
Familiarity with disaster recovery planning concepts and the ability to evaluate disaster recovery program compliance against institutional policy requirements.

Thorough knowledge of one or more cybersecurity compliance frameworks (e.g., ISO 27001/2, NIST 800-171/CMMC, GLBA Safeguards, HIPAA Security Rule, PCI-DSS) and/or institutional Policies for IT/cybersecurity based on standard frameworks.
Ability to monitor and track regulatory developments in information security and privacy laws and assess their implications for institutional compliance programs.

Advanced writing and editing skills, including the proficiency to utilize AI writing tools effectively for drafting, and the ability to produce high-quality technical and non-technical documentation without assistance.
Self-motivated and able to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Able to learn effectively and meet deadlines. Demonstrates problem solving skills.

Demonstrated effective communication and interpersonal skills. Demonstrated ability to communicate technical information to technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization. Interpersonal and communications skills to work with both technical and non-technical personnel at various levels in the organization.

Knowledge of information security concepts, including data classification and security controls, sufficient to evaluate compliance with compliance frameworks and communicate with IT and security teams.
Ability to work across decentralized and distributed organizational structures and stakeholder groups.
